base_prompt: A studio product photo of a rustic terracotta pot with a matching terracotta saucer, filled with dark moist crumbly soil, sitting centered with the base of the pot at the very bottom of the frame. In the middle of the bare soil a single pomegranate seed has just sprouted: a tiny pale hooked sprout tip, faintly reddish at its very end, barely breaking the soil surface. No leaves yet. Real soil texture with a few small clods and a slight sheen of moisture.
style_suffix: Shot as a clean studio product photograph against a seamless pale cream studio background, soft warm diffused daylight, gentle shadows, slight high-angle straight-on view, the terracotta pot centered with its base at the bottom edge of the frame, 3:4 vertical portrait, sharp focus, photorealistic with true-to-life color and natural depth of field. This must look like a REAL pomegranate plant actually photographed in a studio: natural irregular growth, real leaf and soil texture, real terracotta. It is NOT a manicured spherical topiary, NOT a plush or fur-covered ball, NOT plastic or toy-like, NOT cartoonish. No text, no labels, no watermark, no people, no extra props.
edit_prefix: The exact same potted pomegranate in the exact same rustic terracotta pot with dark soil. Keep the pot, the saucer, the camera angle, the soft warm lighting and the seamless pale cream studio background completely identical. Change only the plant by growing it a little more:
edit_suffix: The result must look like a real photographed pomegranate plant with natural irregular branching, real leaf and bark texture, and realistic small pomegranate fruit where present. It is NOT a topiary, NOT a trimmed sphere, NOT plush, NOT fur, NOT plastic or toy-like. Keep it centered with the base of the pot at the bottom of the frame. Photorealistic, 3:4 vertical portrait, no text, no watermark.

growth_deltas.1: the seed splits and a single pale hooked hypocotyl (sprout stem) pushes a little further up out of the soil, still bent over, reddish at the tip.
growth_deltas.2: the hypocotyl straightens upright and lifts two small pale-green cotyledons (seed leaves) just clear of the soil surface.
growth_deltas.3: the two cotyledons widen and deepen to green, and a tiny growing tip becomes visible between them.
growth_deltas.4: the first pair of true leaves emerges from the tip — very small, narrow and oblong, tinted coppery-bronze-red as new pomegranate growth is.
growth_deltas.5: the first true leaves enlarge and begin turning glossy green, while a second pair of small bronze-red leaves starts unfolding at the tip.
growth_deltas.6: the seedling is now a slender stem about 8 to 10 cm tall with two or three pairs of small leaves; the lower leaves are glossy green and the newest top leaves are still bronze-red.
growth_deltas.7: the stem thickens slightly and firms into a faintly woody, grey-tinged base; another leaf pair adds and the seedling stands a touch taller.
growth_deltas.8: a few short side twigs branch out from the lower leaf nodes, each tipped with coppery new growth.
growth_deltas.9: the plant grows bushier as the side twigs lengthen, carrying small clustered opposite leaves; the thin twigs show a faint reddish tint.
growth_deltas.10: it rounds out into a small leafy shrublet about 18 to 20 cm tall; the base of the stem is now clearly woody and grey-brown.
growth_deltas.11: more slender twigs appear, a few ending in the tiny sharp spine typical of pomegranate, and the small-leaved foliage grows denser.
growth_deltas.12: the little bush is a bit taller and fuller with natural irregular branching, coppery new shoots standing out against the glossy green older leaves.
growth_deltas.13: the lower stem bark turns light grey-brown and the canopy broadens unevenly, staying natural and asymmetrical.
growth_deltas.14: it becomes a sturdy little bush about 25 to 28 cm tall with several woody twigs and dense small leaves.
growth_deltas.15: a clear short woody trunk starts to form at the base and the leafy canopy begins to lift slightly off the soil.
growth_deltas.16: the trunk firms and a couple of main branches define a more open shape; more leaves fill in along them.
growth_deltas.17: more side branches and twigs fill the plant out into fuller green foliage, with coppery new tips at the edges.
growth_deltas.18: the young plant grows taller to about 30 to 32 cm with a distinct little trunk and natural irregular branching.
growth_deltas.19: the canopy broadens and thickens with denser glossy green leaves.
growth_deltas.20: the bark on the trunk becomes more textured grey-brown and more fine twigs develop through the crown.
growth_deltas.21: a fuller, rounded-but-natural crown forms, carrying abundant small green leaves.
growth_deltas.22: it clearly reads as a young potted tree now — clear trunk and a leafy canopy — still purely vegetative with no flowers or fruit.
growth_deltas.23: the tree grows taller to about 36 to 38 cm, adding more branches and a finer network of twigs.
growth_deltas.24: the canopy fills in denser and healthier, glossy green with coppery new growth at the tips.
growth_deltas.25: the trunk thickens noticeably and the foliage looks lush and full.
growth_deltas.26: more branching develops and the crown broadens into a fuller, more mature green canopy.
growth_deltas.27: the tree reaches about 44 to 46 cm with a sturdy trunk and a dense leafy crown, still purely vegetative.
growth_deltas.28: the canopy settles into a full rounded-but-irregular green form with robust, healthy foliage.
growth_deltas.29: the trunk is firm grey-brown with a few low side branches, and the whole tree is very leafy.
growth_deltas.30: it is now a real small woody pomegranate tree with a full green canopy — lush glossy leaves, natural irregular branching, and absolutely no flowers and no fruit yet.
growth_deltas.31: the first few swollen, reddish, urn-shaped flower buds appear at the tips of some twigs (still no open flowers).
growth_deltas.32: the first one or two buds open into waxy vermilion-orange tubular trumpet-shaped flowers with a thick fleshy red calyx.
growth_deltas.33: more buds open, giving three to four bright vermilion trumpet blooms scattered naturally over the green foliage.
growth_deltas.34: flowering increases, with several vermilion-orange trumpet flowers across the canopy and more buds forming.
growth_deltas.35: flowering nears its peak — multiple vermilion trumpet flowers dotted naturally through the leaves, and still no fruit at all.
growth_deltas.36: the canopy carries its most flowers yet, vermilion blooms spread through the green foliage — flowers only, no fruit.
growth_deltas.37: the earliest flowers fade and drop their petals, and one or two tiny green fruitlets begin to set, each crowned with the dried leathery calyx.
growth_deltas.38: the green fruitlets swell into small green orbs about 2 cm across with persistent calyx crowns, while a few flowers still remain.
growth_deltas.39: the green fruit grow to about 3 to 4 cm with matte green leathery skin and a clear calyx crown; the last flowers finish.
growth_deltas.40: the green fruit enlarge to about 5 cm, rounder now, smooth green with faint ribbing toward the calyx — still unripe.
growth_deltas.41: the immature fruit reach near full size while still green and leathery-skinned, just one or two main fruit, not yet colored.
growth_deltas.42: a first faint pink-red blush appears on the sunlit side of the largest fruit; there are only one or two fruit on the tree.
growth_deltas.43: the blush deepens to reddish over part of the skin and the leading fruit reaches about 6 cm, its calyx crown persistent.
growth_deltas.44: the leading fruit ripens to a warm reddish-blush pomegranate about 7 cm across while a second fruit stays greenish with a light blush, and the canopy looks fuller.
growth_deltas.45: the first fully ripe red-blush pomegranate hangs from a woody twig with one or two more fruit ripening, and the trunk thickens and turns slightly gnarled.
growth_deltas.46: the trunk becomes thick and gnarled, beginning to look multi-stemmed at the base, beneath a broad mature canopy carrying three to four ripe-and-ripening pomegranates.
growth_deltas.47: it reaches its grand mature size: a thick gnarled multi-stemmed trunk with peeling grey bark and a large naturally irregular spreading canopy of glossy green leaves with coppery new tips, holding three to six small realistic ripe red-blush pomegranates, each about 6 to 8 cm with a persistent calyx crown, hanging naturally among the branches.

wilt_prefix: The exact same potted pomegranate in the exact same rustic terracotta pot, with the pot, saucer, camera angle, soft warm lighting and seamless pale cream studio background all identical, and the plant keeping the same overall size and shape. Only change the health of the foliage:
wilt_suffix: The plant is resting and stressed but still alive in its pot — never a different plant and never an empty pot. It still looks like a real photographed pomegranate, NOT a topiary, NOT plush, NOT plastic. Keep it centered with the base of the pot at the bottom of the frame. Photorealistic, 3:4 vertical portrait, no text, no watermark.

wilt_deltas.1: the very earliest sign of thirst — the leaves droop just slightly and look a touch less glossy than fully healthy, with overall color still mostly green.
wilt_deltas.2: clear wilting now — the leaves droop and soften noticeably, with some yellowing creeping in at the leaf edges and tips.
wilt_deltas.3: the plant looks stressed — many leaves have turned yellow-brown and curled, the foliage droops heavily, a few fallen leaves rest on the soil, and any fruit looks slightly shrivelled.
wilt_deltas.4: severe decline but still alive — most leaves are brown, shrivelled or dropped, the bare twigs droop, and the whole plant has a dry parched look while still standing in the same pot.

notes: PHENOLOGY / TIMING (client's #1 requirement): the journey is vegetative-dominant. Frames 00-30 (~65%) are PURELY VEGETATIVE — seed, sprout, bronze-leaf seedling, bushy young plant, then a real small woody tree with a full green canopy — with NO flowers and NO fruit anywhere. First flowers appear at frame 31 and increase through 36 (still no fruit). Flowers fade and first green immature fruit set at frame 37, swelling green and unripe through 41. Fruit ripens to reddish-blush from frame 42, reaching grand mature canopy at 47. Flowers STRICTLY precede fruit; fruit exists only in roughly the last ~20% of frames. Fruit size stays small and realistic (~6-8 cm, leathery skin, persistent calyx crown) — never giant or cartoonish. Fruit COUNT: 1-2 when first ripening (frames 42-45), building to 3-4 at frame 46 and 3-6 max at frame 47. Flowers are always waxy VERMILION / orange-red tubular trumpet shapes with a thick fleshy calyx. New growth (shoot tips and youngest leaves) is coppery/bronze-red and matures to glossy green; leaves stay small, narrow and oblong-lanceolate, opposite or clustered, on slightly spiny twigs. Bark progresses from green stem to light grey-brown (growing) to textured grey (young tree) to thick gnarled multi-stem grey with peeling bark (mature). Dwarf/patio pomegranate that lives in the pot, so modest in scale. Hard guardrails for the operator: reject any output that looks like a trimmed spherical topiary, a plush/fur ball, plastic/toy foliage, oversized cartoon fruit, or any flower/fruit appearing before its frame — re-roll until it reads as a genuine photographed potted pomegranate at the correct life stage.
